content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Lansing

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires either a bachelor's degree plus three years of project-management experience, or a high school diploma plus five years of experience. Review PMI's official eligibility criteria to confirm you meet the education and experience threshold before enrolling in training.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP Certification Training course. Attend sessions on your schedule, ask questions in real time, and receive direct instruction from active certified practitioners. All training is delivered online, making it convenient for Lansing professionals balancing work and development.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After completing your 35 contact hours, submit your PMP application directly to PMI, including proof of your education and project-management experience. Pay PMI's exam fee at the time of application. PMI will review and approve your eligibility before you can schedule your exam.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the PMP Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources, practice exams, and study materials to solidify your knowledge of the PMBOK® Guide and project-management domains. Schedule your proctored exam when ready. The PMP exam tests your mastery of core project-management concepts and real-world application.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: After earning your PMP, commit to a three-year renewal cycle. Earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) through approved training, certifications, volunteering, or work experience. Renew your credential on time to keep it active and demonstrate ongoing professional commitment to employers in Lansing's competitive job market.

fq_items.question: What are the PMP eligibility requirements?
fq_items.answer: PMI sets four eligibility paths based on education: a secondary diploma (high school or equivalent) requires 60 months of project leadership experience; an associate's degree requires 48 months; a bachelor's degree requires 36 months; and a bachelor's or postgraduate degree from a PMI Global Accreditation Center (GAC)-accredited program requires just 24 months. Every path also requires 35 hours of project management education — our course satisfies this requirement in full.

fq_items.question: How long does it take to get PMP certified in {city}?
fq_items.answer: After completing training, PMI typically approves applications within 5–10 business days. Once approved, you have one year to sit for the exam. Most students study 4–8 weeks after the course before scheduling their exam.

fq_items.question: What is your pass guarantee?
fq_items.answer: If you complete our course and do not pass the PMP exam within 90 days, we provide additional coaching sessions at no additional cost until you pass.
